classification.difficultyReason: Convert elapsed hours to doubling periods, use the resulting exponent in a threshold inequality, and convert the logarithmic result to minutes.

content.prompt: A bacterial population starts with 1000 bacteria and doubles every half hour.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many bacteria are there after 2 hours?

answer.worked:
There are four half-hour periods in 2 hours.

$$\begin{align*}P(2)&=1000\times 2^4\\P(2)&=16\,000\end{align*}$$

There are 16 000 bacteria.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Write down a general equation for the population of the bacteria after $t$ hours.

answer.worked:
There are two half-hour periods per hour, so the exponent is $2t$.

$$P(t)=1000\times 2^{2t}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: How long will it be until the population exceeds 1 million? Round to the nearest minute.

answer.short: 4 hours and 59 minutes, to the nearest minute.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}1000\times 2^{2t}&>1\,000\,000\\2^{2t}&>1000\\2t\ln 2&>\ln 1000\\t&>\frac{\ln 1000}{2\ln 2}\end{align*}$$

The threshold time in minutes is

$$\begin{align*}T&=60\times\frac{\ln 1000}{2\ln 2}\\T&\approx 298.97.\end{align*}$$

The population exceeds 1 million just after this threshold, which rounds to 4 hours and 59 minutes.
